title: Allocating Scarce Resources Under Real Constraints
description: Practice making advanced resource allocation decisions involving capacity limits, opportunity costs, and strategic sequencing.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company has 3 engineering teams. Team A: 95% utilized, 12% revenue impact. Team B: 60% utilized, 41% revenue impact. Team C: 80% utilized, 47% revenue impact. Which is the biggest allocation red flag?

options.text: Team A is over-utilized on low-impact work
Team B has idle capacity on highest-impact work
Team C needs more headcount immediately
All teams are properly allocated

interactions.prompt: Your logistics startup has $400K left this quarter. Option 1: Hire 4 warehouse ops staff to cut fulfillment delays by 30%. Option 2: Build an AI routing tool (6-month payoff) projected to cut costs 22% annually. You're losing 8% of customers monthly to slow delivery.

options.text: Hire all 4 ops staff now to stop customer bleeding
Build the AI tool for larger long-term savings
Hire 2 ops staff, allocate remaining $200K to AI tool
Outsource fulfillment temporarily and invest fully in AI

interactions.prompt: When a team is at 100% utilization with no slack, the hidden cost is lost ____, because they cannot respond to urgent high-value opportunities without dropping existing commitments.

options.text: Option value
Sunk cost
Fixed overhead
Variable margin

interactions.prompt: Stripe's platform team has capacity for only 2 of 4 projects this quarter. Rank by allocation priority: (a) Refactor legacy payments API (tech debt, saves 15 eng-hrs/week), (b) Launch enterprise dashboard (pipeline: $8M ARR, 3-month build), (c) Fix recurring checkout bug (2% cart abandonment impact), (d) Build partner integration (signed LOI worth $3M ARR, 6-week build).

options.text: Refactor legacy payments API
Launch enterprise dashboard
Fix recurring checkout bug
Build partner integration

interactions.prompt: A CPG brand allocates marketing spend: Digital ads ($500K, ROAS 4.2x), TV ($1.2M, ROAS 1.8x), Influencers ($300K, ROAS 5.1x), Trade promos ($700K, ROAS 2.3x). Total budget is fixed at $2.7M. What should change?

options.text: Cut TV spend and redistribute to digital and influencers
Double down on TV for broader brand awareness
Eliminate trade promos entirely
Allocate equally across all four channels

interactions.prompt: You lead product at a fintech with 12 engineers. A regulator just mandated a compliance feature (requires 5 engineers, 8 weeks). You're mid-sprint on a growth feature (7 engineers, 4 weeks left) projected to add $1.2M ARR. Compliance deadline is 10 weeks out.

options.text: Pause growth feature, shift all 12 engineers to compliance
Finish growth feature in 4 weeks, then pivot all to compliance
Split: keep 5 on growth, move 7 to compliance now
Outsource compliance to a contractor team entirely

interactions.prompt: A hospital system must sequence four capital projects with a $10M annual budget: (a) New MRI machine ($3M, 14-month ROI, aging current unit), (b) ER expansion ($5M, reduces wait times 40%, 3-year ROI), (c) Cybersecurity upgrade ($1.5M, audit flagged critical vulnerabilities), (d) Telehealth platform ($2M, projected 20% patient volume increase, 18-month ROI). Rank by optimal sequencing.

options.text: New MRI machine
ER expansion
Cybersecurity upgrade
Telehealth platform

interactions.prompt: Your largest customer (18% of revenue) just threatened to churn in 60 days unless you deliver a custom analytics module. Your engineering team is fully committed to the compliance and growth roadmap you just sequenced. What do you do?

options.text: Pull engineers off growth to build the custom module
Negotiate a partial solution using existing features plus a contractor
Let the customer churn to protect your roadmap
Delay the compliance deadline to free up capacity

interactions.priorContext: You previously decided to finish your growth feature in 4 weeks then pivot all engineers to a mandatory compliance build. Your team is at full capacity with zero slack. Now a major revenue-critical customer demands custom work on the same timeline.
